Description: Patient identity verification and administrative intake at the admissions desk.
Nurse-led initial assessment to assign priority level using standardised triage protocol.
Initial physician assessment of patient condition and determination of investigation plan.
Collection and analysis of blood samples for biochemical and haematological markers.
Plain radiographic imaging of the requested body region.
Computed tomography imaging; typically used for complex or high-priority presentations.
Electrocardiogram recording to assess cardiac rhythm and electrical activity.
Ultrasound imaging for soft-tissue and abdominal assessment.
Administration of therapeutic interventions including medication, wound care, or procedures.
Referral and handover to an inpatient or outpatient specialist team.
Follow-up clinical assessment after initial treatment or investigation results.
Preparation and administration of prescribed medications by nursing staff.
Formal admission to an inpatient ward following clinical decision.
Patient transfer to another ward, unit, or external facility.
Completion of administrative discharge process and provision of after-care instructions.
Structured pain scoring using a validated scale (e.g., NRS).
Insertion of an intravenous cannula for fluid or medication delivery.
Monitored waiting period for condition evolution before further decision.
Referral to social work team for safeguarding, housing, or discharge planning needs.
Coordination of post-discharge care, prescriptions, and follow-up appointments.
